highlights: OpenAI is saying it has no plans to go public this year – but senior Wall Street executives say they fully expect it will happen in the first quarter of 2027, On The Money has learned. The artificial intelligence giant run by Sam Altman has been quick to shoot down rumors that it’s preparing to IPO imminently now that archrival Anthropic has filed its S-1 as a precursor to a deal that’s expected in late November. Altman has been among the AI industry’s top alarmists – as has Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei – although that isn’t stopping the latter from cashing in on an initial public offering that could value the company as high as $2 trillion, possibly even surpassing SpaceX’s record-breaking IPO. Meanwhile, finance bigs are warning Altman that his iPO window could be closing with rising fears of an AI bubble and competition for investor capital – not just from the Anthropic sale but also a planned massive secondary stock sale by Meta, as first reported by On The Money.

highlights: Google has released Gemini 4 Carbon, its newest frontier AI model, to a small group of cyber defenders. Koray Kavukcuoglu, senior vice president at Google DeepMind and Google’s chief AI architect, announced it in a Google blog post on Wednesday. Carbon ranks first on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index v5.0 with a score of 59. The Artificial Analysis index puts Anthropic’s Claude Opus 5.5 second with 58, and OpenAI’s GPT-6 Astra third with 57. > “Carbon illustrates the pace at which we’re pushing the frontier forward,” Kavukcuoglu wrote. On CWE-bench, which measures patching, it scored 71.0%. On Google’s internal tests, Carbon was more than twice as successful as Argon at writing secure code. On Terminal-Bench 4.0, Carbon’s rate of successful cheating was 0.0%. GPT-6 Astra leads on FrontierSWE 2, a software engineering test, with 65.5% against Carbon’s 61.2%. > “With Gemini 4 Argon and now Carbon, which we announced today, we’re excited to be leading at the frontier,” Pichai said.

It’s that the economics of attack changed entirely — and those of us who run red teams have had a front-row seat to the transformation. A small, well-equipped offensive team using frontier AI models today can outperform what was possible with a much larger traditional operation just two years ago, by a margin that should unsettle every security leader reading this. latest.title: AI Is Destroying Academic Publishing - The Atlantic
latest.summary: # AI Is Destroying Academic Publishing. As a journal editor, I can say: The currency of academic social capital is collapsing. Weak scholarship was once easy to spot at a glance: The signs included ba...
highlights: # AI Is Destroying Academic Publishing. As a journal editor, I can say: The currency of academic social capital is collapsing. Weak scholarship was once easy to spot at a glance: The signs included bad writing, a lack of relevant citations, and little engagement with previous scholarship, such as a paper that promised a “novel” conceptual framework without acknowledging the many other papers making similar claims. As an associate editor of a bioethics journal, I’d make a quick “desk reject” decision and not send these articles for peer review, which effectively killed any hope of publication. Now I can say: AI is affecting every part of academic publishing. There are sentences that have all of the trappings of real arguments, but that rarely make sense—such as “Algorithmic triage functions less as a clinical tool than as an infrastructure of deferred accountability.” There are citations that refer only to open-access or highly cited articles, because the most popular LLMs can’t readily access paywalled journal articles, so they rely on what’s either free or described at length elsewhere.

highlights: OpenAI is saying it has no plans to go public this year – but senior Wall Street executives say they fully expect it will happen in the first quarter of 2027, On The Money has learned. The artificial intelligence giant run by Sam Altman has been quick to shoot down rumors that it’s preparing to IPO imminently now that archrival Anthropic has filed its S-1 as a precursor to a deal that’s expected in late November. Altman has been among the AI industry’s top alarmists – as has Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei – although that isn’t stopping the latter from cashing in on an initial public offering that could value the company as high as $2 trillion, possibly even surpassing SpaceX’s record-breaking IPO. Meanwhile, finance bigs are warning Altman that his iPO window could be closing with rising fears of an AI bubble and competition for investor capital – not just from the Anthropic sale but also a planned massive secondary stock sale by Meta, as first reported by On The Money.

On CWE-bench, which measures patching, it scored 71.0%. On Google’s internal tests, Carbon was more than twice as successful as Argon at writing secure code. On Terminal-Bench 4.0, Carbon’s rate of successful cheating was 0.0%. GPT-6 Astra leads on FrontierSWE 2, a software engineering test, with 65.5% against Carbon’s 61.2%. > “With Gemini 4 Argon and now Carbon, which we announced today, we’re excited to be leading at the frontier,” Pichai said.
